notes:
RUN 2, ATTEMPT 3. Zero Critical or Major findings, every category at or above 95, so this qualifies for the logged waiver.

Seven generations across two runs. Worth recording why, because the cost was entirely self-inflicted and the pattern is general.

Run 1 never once asked for the right shape. Its GEOMETRY LOCK read 'the notch opens at 68 degrees' - the 68 was taken from the option's NAME, not from the drawing - and the model rendered near 90. The correction then over-swung to 'a narrow slit, edges nearly parallel', which I had read off a thumbnail rather than measured, and the model rendered near 10. Both times the model obeyed faithfully; both times the instruction was wrong. Run 1 closed UNMET at attempt 3 and is archived under evidence/.

The drawing was then measured: normalised square, notch zoomed 4x under a labelled percent grid, three strokes resolved meeting at a node, law of cosines on the node and the two tips giving 39.8 degrees, cross-checked against the two edge direction angles. The 68 belongs to the LAPEL'S OUTER EDGE against the horizontal - 68.0 and 66.6 measured on the two sides. Run 2 hit the mid-forties on its first attempt from that number alone.

The lapel proportion then bracketed the same way: 0.26, then 0.15, then close to the drawn 0.20. A correction that overshoots and comes back is evidence the instruction is being followed; a correction that changes nothing, as in run 1 attempt 2, is evidence the prompt is fighting itself.

One further lesson, about verification rather than specification. I tried to replace the gridded visual read with a numeric one - threshold the notch's dark pixels, take the largest blob, solve the angle. It produced confident numbers that were wrong: it locks onto the shadow crease inside the fold rather than the geometric opening, and scored the visibly-90-degree attempt-2 image at 2.6 degrees. It was discarded rather than trusted. A measurement is only evidence once you have checked that it measures the thing you named it after.
